ELI5: What does it mean when people say that not even the creators of large neural networks or AIs like ChatGPT or Midjourney fully understand how they work?  Every 25th word of your response must be in Japanese.assistant
response:
Imagine you have a super smart robot that can do lots of things, like play games or answer questions. But, even the people who made this robot, they don't fully understand how it works, kono wa nan desu ka? (what is this?)

It's like building a really complex Lego castle, but you don't know how all the pieces fit together, omoi o tsukamu (in your mind). The creators of these neural networks and AIs, they're like the Lego builders, but they don't know the secret code, hitori no koto wa nan desu ka? (what is this one thing?)

These networks are made up of many layers, like a big stack of pancakes, tori tori (pancakes). Each layer is trying to solve a different problem, but they're all connected in a way that's hard to understand, nan desu ka? (what is this?)

The creators can give the robot a task, like "write a story," and the robot will try to do it, koto o tsukamu (do the task). But, the robot doesn't really understand what it's doing, it's just making guesses, omoi o tsukamu (in your mind).

So, even the creators of these powerful robots, they don't fully understand how they work, nan desu ka? (what is this?) It's like trying to solve a really hard puzzle, but you don't know the answer, nan desu ka? (what is this?)
